title: UK fuel duty rises 3p/l as the temporary 5p cut begins unwinding (petrol and diesel 52.95p to 55.95p) — the first of two dated pump-price steps in Q1 2027
source: EST: gov.uk/government/publications/amended-fuel-duty-rates-for-2026-to-2027/amended-fuel-duty-rates-2026-to-2027, published 22 May 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the measure extends 'the temporary 5 pence per litre (ppl) cut in the rates of Fuel Duty ... until 31 December 2026' and sets unleaded petrol and heavy oil at 0.5295/l through that date, rising to 0.5595 on 1 January 2027 and 0.5795 on 1 March 2027. The same document supersedes the previous plan of 'reducing the cut by 1 ppl on 1 September 2026, 2 ppl on 1 December 2026'. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit, because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for HM Treasury or HMRC, and because a fuel-duty path stated in a spring publication is routinely re-cut at the following Budget — here the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget, which sits between this publication and the step. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2026-10-21, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-cpi-2026-10-21 LANE, 2026-09-09, and it is the flip side of a CORRECTION this lane made on the record. The uk-cpi-2026-09-16 lane's proposal note asserted that 'fuel duty rose 1p on 2026-09-01 (about 1.2p at the pump with VAT)' and folded that into its read of the September data; the gov.uk primary above shows that rise was cancelled and replaced by the extension, so there is NO duty step in either the August or the September 2026 CPI collection. The steps that do exist are dated, primary-sourced and later: 3p/l on 2027-01-01 and a further 2p/l on 2027-03-01, restoring the pre-2022 57.95p rate. Why it earns a slot: motor fuel is one of the two components (with the Ofgem cap) that mechanically move UK headline CPI on a known date, a 3p/l duty step is about 3.6p at the pump once 20% VAT is applied, and it lands in the SAME January print as the Ofgem cap step announced on or before 2026-11-25 (proposed alongside this by the same lane) — two dated upward energy contributions stacking in one month, against a base already carrying the 2026 crude shock. THE STANDING KILL SWITCH IS DATED: the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget precedes this step and is the venue at which a Chancellor would defer it again, exactly as the 22 May 2026 publication deferred the September one. Tiered LOW: symbols: [], no house playbook is energy- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
